items.note: Quasi-experiment with 96 graphic design students in a control and an experimental (generative AI) group, with pretest/posttest originality and design-thinking rubrics scored by two external judges; non-random assignment, so likely fails the randomization criterion; abstract in Spanish.

Randomised controlled trial of ChatGPT versus no ChatGPT with 1190 business undergraduates in three disciplines, scoring fluency, originality, and elaboration of their output; online 2025, 2026 issue.

Within-subjects experiment where 36 participants designed advertisements with and without generative AI, with creativity, usefulness, and appeal rated by clients and online volunteers; below 50 participants and order randomization not stated (abstract via Semantic Scholar).

Between-subjects study (n = 253) of short essay writing with AI support at the planning, drafting, or revising stage; main outcome is self-reported ownership, but the abstract also reports essay quality, and the next stage should check whether a no-AI arm exists and whether quality is rated.

Online experiment in which 276 people refined innovation-challenge ideas alone or with AI-generated text or images, with idea creativity and effort measured; random assignment not stated in the abstract.

Systematic literature review on generative AI and the creative thinking of STEAM learners in higher education; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect 403), classified from the title.

Controlled experiment with 40 Chinese GFL undergraduates assigned to human-only, human-LLM, or LLM-only writing, with Torrance-style creativity rubric scores; below 50 participants and assignment method not stated.

Observational analysis of 41.3 million natural-science papers relating AI-augmented research to scientists' impact and to a narrowing of collective topic breadth; AI tools span distinct eras of AI, not generative AI specifically, so scope needs checking.

Human-AI complementarities in innovation search, likely from Hassan's Nord University dissertation; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect 403), so design is unknown and classified as experiment only by the doubt rule.

Two-player Alternate Uses Test platform comparing co-creation with a GPT-4 partner versus a human partner, plus non-interactive baselines, in an in-person pilot (N = 62) with originality scored; the comparison is AI partner versus human partner, and assignment is not stated.
